Villagers are automatically recruited from the Town Center at no cost whenever there is spare Villager Capacity. Start: 6 Villagers, capacity 10. Each Longhouse adds +10 Villager Capacity and +25 max population. The HUD warns 'Villager capacity almost reached build more Longhouses' and then 'Villager capacity reached build more Longhouses'. Falkr's Village Saga reduces Villager recruitment time by 2 seconds.
Consume Food from the target Food source to heal yourself. Consume 1 Food every 3 seconds to regain 0.4 health per second. Automatically improves with each Age.
Influence: The cost of ships in all Docks are reduced by 4% for each Longhouse within influence of any Dock up to a maximum of 16%.
Sagas are quests that can be completed at any time which will unlock permanent bonuses.
Complete this Saga by regaining 1000 health on Infantry. Saga reward: All Infantry gain 10% health and charge range is increased by 2 tiles.
Complete this Saga by upgrading 6 Longhouses with attachments. Saga reward: Villager production speed reduced by 2 seconds and reduced Longhouse attachment cost by 20%.
Complete this Saga by destroying 2 Technology or Economy buildings. Saga reward: All technologies cost 15% less and Smithy/Loom research 45 seconds faster.
Complete this Saga by earning 1000 Gold by Traders or Trade Ships. Saga reward: Ships and Siege Weapons cost 8% less.
Complete this Saga by gathering 2500 Food from Boar, Deer, or Shore Fish with Villagers. Saga reward: Villagers gather 10% faster and get +5 carry capacity.
Complete this Saga by recruiting 25 infantry. Saga reward: Melee Infantry gain +5 torch damage and +1 tile torch attack range.
Complete this Saga by constructing the Gullinn Temple Landmark. Saga reward: Sacred Groves produce Berserkers 15% faster.
Units near the Sacred Grove gain +1 melee and ranged armor.

Both Age IV landmarks increase population and maximum population by +10, so max population goes from 200 to 210. Kongens Dør Cathedral (Age IV Economic Landmark) acts as a Monastery and has a unique technology (Folkekirken) that adds another +10, for 220. Rikets Nyckel Castle (Age IV Defensive Landmark) gives +10 only (210).

In Castle Age (III) the Vikings get two cheaper, weaker variants of standard units. The Stable gets the Jylland Knight (Heavy Melee Cavalry, 120 food 90 gold, 'Lower cost but with reduced damage and health', grants 10 Gold on death). The Archery Range gets Skåne Crossbowmen (Light Ranged Infantry, 75 food 30 gold, 'Lower cost but with reduced damage and health'). Both read 'Requirements: Castle Age (III)'.

Longhouses can be upgraded with one of four different attachments. The Farmstead adds two vegetable fields, which have a higher gather rate than normal Farms. The Bee Skeps will passively generate gold. Looms will automatically improve the armor of military units. The Smithy will automatically improve the damage of military units.

Völur are support units that can travel between Longhouses, boosting the production of Bee Skeps and Farmsteads for a duration. The Völur can also be sacrificed to establish a Sacred Grove on Relics, which passively recruits Berserkers and has an aura that increases the armor of nearby units.
Bondi are unique spearmen that have increased health and armor. When Bondi are near each other, they gain a Shield Wall buff temporarily increasing their health.

The Longship is a unique archer ship that also acts as a transport, each loaded unit increases the arrows fired and increases health. The Drakkar replaces the Springald Ship and can throw nets on enemy ships to slow them down.

Has a large line of sight and adds 3 muster charges for the Mustering Hall or Three Loch Lookout. The number of warriors received from mustering is increased by 75%. Comes with the option to muster a navy if constructed adjacent to water.
Protect Highland Cattle grazing in berry bushes; they provide food continuously as they eat. Herd capacity increases with each Highland landmark built.

Highland Cattle sustain themselves at Berry Bushes for Food. While eating they produce Food at a rate of 30 per minute. They begin with a capacity of 9, and that increases by 4 with every Highland Landmark built.

Infantry have a deep knowledge of and connection to the land, gaining advantages when fighting in and around Dense Forests. They ignore the sight penalty when entering Dense Forests and gain movement speed while Highland Ambush is active.
Tower Houses replace Outposts, can produce Highland Cattle and Ghillies, and raise the population cap.
In the Feudal Age (Age II), warriors can be quickly mustered at the Mustering Hall.

Naval arrowslits are 50% cheaper.

When a Keep is destroyed it uses scorched-earth tactics, damaging the surrounding area for a time. Enemies in the area have their combat ability temporarily reduced. The Keep becomes Castle Ruins, which can be repaired in time to avoid total destruction. Castle Ruins can be fully repaired for at most 600 stone; repairs after that are free.

Each time you age up you choose a Highland or Lowland landmark. The Mustering Hall has unique technologies from these regions. As landmarks are built in a region, that region's technologies cost half to support its development.

Building military buildings around the Mustering Hall raises its tier, making mustered warriors more efficient. Tier 1: unlocks mustering Highland Archers and +1 muster charge. Tier 2: lower muster cost and +1 muster charge. Tier 3: lower muster cost, +1 muster charge, and mustered warriors gain health.
